name: Run a week of your life
intro: The one cross-lane capstone. Lane finales prove skills one lane at a time; real life arrives all at once. This is the dress rehearsal for launch — and the only node that belongs to every lane and none.
gotItWhen: For one real week, the whole machine is yours at once — you feed yourself, run your money, get yourself everywhere you're going, keep your appointments and deadlines, handle whatever paperwork the week brings — and when something goes sideways mid-week (something always does), you absorb it, adjust, and keep the week on the rails, with the adults strictly on-call and hearing about most of it afterward.
looksLike: Meals happen from your plan and your cooking, the budget holds, and you're on time to the things you committed to — all in the same seven days.
The week's admin — a form, a refill, a bill, a booking — gets handled by you, in the gaps, without the week derailing.
The surprise arrives — a canceled ride, a dead phone, a schedule collision, a burned dinner — and the family hears how you solved it after it's already solved.
waysToBuild: Schedule it like a real event during ordinary life — school, activities, everything running — not during a quiet vacation week.
Agree the scope up front with your parents: the budget, the check-in rhythm, and what genuinely counts as call-us territory.
Debrief once at the end as colleagues: what ran itself, what leaked, and which lane the leaks point back to.
